title: Carbon recipe
description: A layout, flow, widget or draft pattern written as data: a tree of real Carbon and labs components, placed on Carbon's grid and spaced with Carbon's spacing tokens, with no literal values. Rendered by @carbon-labs/react-recipe-renderer and checked by recipe-lint (ADR 0009, decision 5). Every field below says why it exists; a field that cannot say so does not belong here.

$schema.description: Points at this file, so an editor validates and completes a recipe as it is written. Recipes in the renderer package use "../recipe.schema.json".

name.description: The recipe's identity for tooling: the file is <name>.recipe.json, the story is named from it, and the registry of recipes is keyed by it.

kind.description: Which building-* recipe governs it, and therefore which rubric a review applies. A flow has steps; every other kind has a tree. pattern-draft is a pattern still evolving as data before it is built as a labs component (building-patterns).

status.description: The labs lifecycle, as a component's package.json labs.status carries it. preview means a person has reviewed the recipe against the rubric; nothing self-promotes.

description.description: One or two sentences a person reads in Storybook. What the screen is for, not what is on it.

tree.description: The composition, for every kind but flow.

steps.description: A flow's screens, one at a time. The first step is where the flow starts.

meta.description: Borrowed from writing-metadata so a recipe is SELECTABLE: an agent or an MCP client chooses a recipe the way it chooses a component, by intent and useWhen, and is stopped by preferInstead. Only the three selection fields; the rest of the object metadata (checks, divergence, a11y) belongs to components.

intent.description: One sentence naming what the user gets, not what is drawn.

useWhen.description: The conditions that select this recipe.

preferInstead.description: The better answer and when it is better. The field that catches the plausible choice.

component.description: "<package>:<Export>" — the package a person would import from and the name it exports. A preview namespace member is written "@carbon/react:preview__Dialog.Dialog". recipe-lint resolves it against the installed package; the renderer looks it up in an explicit registry.

props.description: The component's props, as JSON. Text content is props.children. A handler is { "$event": "<name>" }, which the renderer turns into a function that raises that event. style and className are refused: a recipe adds no styling of its own.

slot.description: Render this node into the parent's prop of this name instead of its children — for the Carbon props that take a node (a Tile's title, a notification's actions).

grid.description: Place this node in a Carbon Column of the parent Grid. Spans per breakpoint, in Carbon's column counts (sm 4, md 8, lg/xlg/max 16).

gap.description: Space between this node's children, as a Carbon spacing token. Rendered by Carbon's own Stack (gap 5 is $spacing-05), so the recipe adds no CSS for it.

padding.description: Space inside this node, as a Carbon spacing token. Rendered as a wrapper whose padding is that $spacing token.

radius.description: This node's corner radius, as a Carbon border-radius token. It goes on the component's own element, not a wrapper, because the radius must cut the surface the component paints. The design law assigns a rung per role (ibm-design-rules › shape.md): containers 8, modals 16, fields 6, controls full — a container left square has left the ladder.

fill.description: Make this node fill what it sits in, for the one case a recipe cannot express with spacing: a shell that must occupy the screen. "viewport" is the screen's height, "parent" is the height of the node above, and "scroll" is the node that absorbs the overflow — it takes the space its siblings leave and scrolls its own content, so a long transcript scrolls inside the shell instead of pushing the composer off the screen. A filling shell needs exactly one scroller on each branch that can overflow. Height only — width already fills, and a recipe never sets a width.

measure.description: Cap this node at a named reading measure and centre it. A recipe names the role, never a number, so the column a person reads is one decision in one place: the transcript, the composer, the traces and the notices all take the same measure instead of each carrying a width. "reading" is the chat reading column. Inline only — a recipe never sets a height, and `fill` is what answers that question.

theme.description: Put this node, and everything in it, in a polarity named by ROLE rather than by name, so one recipe is both the light screen and the dark one. "chrome" is the shell — the rail, the top band, the docked toolbar — which is dark in both polarities, as Carbon's own UI Shell is: chrome does not follow the theme, it frames whatever does. "page" is the work surface, which does follow it: a light card inside the chrome on a light page, and a dark one on a dark page. Use this instead of naming @carbon/react:Theme with an absolute theme: that pins the screen to one polarity and the other one stops existing.

surface.description: Which elevation this node rests on, inside whatever polarity it is in — the rung, where `theme` is the polarity. "base" is the content canvas and "raised" is a card or panel one step up, painted with Carbon's own layer token so the step is Carbon's and not a value written here. A rung is static: a component knows it when it is written, so this is never resolved from runtime context. Pair it with `radius`, which cuts the surface this paints.

children.description: Nodes rendered inside this one, in order.

step.description: One screen of a flow, and where each of its events goes.

id.description: The step's name, which on targets point at.

on.description: event name -> the id of the step it moves to. A step with no on is terminal.

spacingToken.description: A Carbon spacing token name, exactly as @carbon/layout names it (spacing-01 … spacing-13). recipe-lint checks it exists in the installed @carbon/layout.

radiusToken.description: A Carbon border-radius token name, exactly as @carbon/layout names it (border-radius-00 … border-radius-24, border-radius-max). recipe-lint checks it exists in the installed @carbon/layout, so the ladder is Carbon's and no radius is written here.
